title: Retry loop and circuit breaker
idea: The core `ApiClient` runs a bounded retry loop: attempts share one deadline, waits grow exponentially with jitter, and a circuit breaker stops calls to a failing service.

analogy.text: Phoning a busy shop. You wait longer between each try, give up by closing time, and stop calling for a while after it keeps failing.
analogy.breaks: A shop cannot tell you how long to wait; servers sometimes can.

points: The deadline is fixed at the start; each attempt gets at most what remains.
Backoff doubles each attempt up to a cap; jitter spreads callers apart.
The client stops early when the next wait would pass the deadline.
The breaker opens after repeated failures, then lets one trial call through.

steps.caption: The caller asks for one order. The client fixes a total deadline now.
Attempt 1: the breaker is closed, so the call goes ahead.
The transport sends the request with a per-attempt timeout.
The service answers 503. That failure is transient, and GET is safe to repeat.
The client waits a jittered backoff, then sends attempt 2.
No answer arrives before the attempt timeout. The transport gives up and reports TIMEOUT.
A longer wait, then attempt 3 reaches a recovered service.
200 comes back. The caller sees one successful call, not three attempts.

code.title: Retry loop with deadline
code.caption: Three calls against a scripted service: a recovery, a refused POST retry, and a budget that runs out. The breaker is left out to keep the loop short; BreakerCore shows it alone, and it plugs in before each attempt.

walk.text: The fake service answers a status after some milliseconds, or never, which costs the full attempt timeout.
Four attempts, backoff from 100 ms up to 1000 ms, 300 ms per try, 1500 ms in all.
Fix the deadline once; each attempt gets the smaller of its timeout and the time left.
The policy says stop: success, a permanent error, an unsafe request, or attempts used up.
Never sleep past the deadline; return the last result instead.
Double per attempt up to the cap, keep half, randomise the other half.

code.title: Circuit breaker states
code.caption: Three failures open the breaker. After the cool-down one trial goes through; its result closes or reopens it. The mode stays OPEN until the next call asks; that call moves it to HALF_OPEN, so the failed trial prints OPEN again.

walk.text: Open after 3 failures, stay open for 5000 ms, then replay a script of events.
While open, a call is refused without touching the network.
When the cool-down has passed, move to HALF_OPEN and allow the trial.
Any success closes the breaker and clears the failure count.
A failed trial reopens at once; otherwise open when failures reach the threshold.

pitfalls: Without jitter, clients that failed together retry together and overload the service again.
Cap each attempt by the time left; per-attempt timeouts alone let retries overrun the total.
This breaker is not thread-safe: two threads seeing OPEN after cool-down both send trials.

quiz.q: What does ApiClientCore print for the POST /orders call?
options: #1 503 and nothing else for that call
quiz.why: POST without an Idempotency-Key is not safe to repeat. The policy refuses the retry, so the 503 returns at once.

takeaway: Bound retries by a deadline, spread them with jitter, stop calling sick services.

starters: Why equal jitter here instead of full jitter?
Should a breaker count timeouts the same as 503s?
How do I pick the failure threshold and cool-down time?
